paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: humility is not thinking less of yourself, it's looking out for somebody else. Paul says to do nothing out of "selfish ambition or empty pride," but in humility to "consider others more important than yourselves" (Philippians 2:3). Then he adds that each of us should look "not only to your own interests, but also to the interests of others" (Philippians 2:4). Not NONE of your own, friend, just not ONLY your own.

And Paul doesn't leave us with a rule, he points us to a Person. Christ Jesus existed in the form of God, yet He "emptied Himself, taking the form of a servant," and "became obedient to death—even death on a cross" (Philippians 2:7-8). Then comes that big "Therefore": God exalted Him to the highest place, and every tongue will confess that Jesus Christ is Lord (Philippians 2:9-11). The way down was the way God chose, so when you pick the lowest seat for someone else's sake, you are walking where Jesus already walked.

So how do we live that out on a Monday? Paul says to keep working out your salvation, and then he drops the best news: "it is God who works in you to will and to act on behalf of His good purpose" (Philippians 2:12-13). You are not doing this on your own strength, friend, because He supplies the want-to AND the can-do. So do everything without complaining or arguing, shine like a light, hold forth the word of life, and be glad, because Paul was glad in chains and he wants you glad too (Philippians 2:14-18).
